title: Lift Yourself
annotation:
In April 2018 Kanye tweeted for days about a song that would answer his critics. The answer was 'Lift Yourself': a gorgeous Amnesty soul loop, a minute of build, and then roughly thirty seconds of improvised syllables about scooping poop, delivered with total conviction.

It is the most famous troll in hip-hop history and the clearest statement of this site's thesis: a rapper at the height of his powers, with the world's attention, chose poop. It is the national anthem of Poop Rhymes and will remain number one until something tops it. Nothing will.
note: The entire vocal is nonsense syllables built around scooping and pooping, over a soul loop that deserved better and got exactly what it needed.

title: Think U the Shit (Fart)
annotation:
A diss track whose entire thesis is a fart joke: the target thinks they're the best, but they're actually just gas. The parenthetical in the title does the work of a whole verse.

It debuted on the Billboard Hot 100, which means a song with 'fart' in its official title was a chart hit in 2024. The Source pointed out the bar closely echoes a J. Cole line from 2011 (see 'Dollar and a Dream III'), which is the first time a fart joke has had a documented lineage.
note: Hook built on the contrast between being the shit and being a fart; the fart is the target.

title: T.S.R. (Toilet Stool Rap)
annotation:
The founding text. Biz dedicates an entire song to writing his rhymes on the toilet, complete with rules of bathroom etiquette, and does it with the same goofy warmth he brought to everything.

Vice's history of poop rap traces the genre to this track, and there's a credible claim that Run from Run-DMC wrote hits on the toilet too. Biz just had the nerve to say so on record. Everything on this site descends from T.S.R.
note: A whole song about composing rhymes while sitting on the toilet, with bathroom rules.

title: A Milli
annotation:
Lil Wayne is the undisputed king of this genre. Vice counted 99 separate poop references across his catalog, and that was in 2013. 'A Milli', the mixtape-energy single that made Tha Carter III a phenomenon, has one of the best: a bowel-trouble taunt dropped in among the money talk like it's nothing.

The Wayne method is to treat poop as just another word in the punchline toolkit, no more or less special than guns or cars. That's why he has 99 of these and everyone else has two.
note: A bowel-trouble taunt aimed at rivals, mid-boast.

title: Ether
annotation:
One of the most celebrated diss tracks ever recorded contains a fart joke. Nas, mid-evisceration of Jay-Z, compares his verbal assault to a slow-burning fart: the kind that lingers.

The fact that 'Ether' entered the language as a verb for destroying someone, and that the song doing it has a flatulence bar, is the whole reason this site exists.
note: A joke about a slow-burning fart, used as a metaphor for how the diss lingers.

title: Dog Shit
annotation:
ODB in full dog persona, on a double album that sold like a pop record. The song is exactly what the title says, delivered with the unhinged commitment only Dirty could manage, and Method Man shows up to narrate the scene like a nature documentary.

Not safe for anyone, and one of the purest expressions of the Wu-Tang belief that nothing was off-limits if it was funny enough.
note: ODB adopts a dog-pooping persona in a sexual scenario; Method Man provides commentary.

title: Shit on You
annotation:
The lead single from D12's debut, and the moment Eminem's poop fixation got a hook. The threat is literal: he will defecate on your possessions as revenge. Proof, Bizarre and Kuniva take it from there.

Eminem has returned to this well for twenty-plus years (see 'So Far...', 'Just Lose It', 'My 1st Single', 'Caterpillar'). This is where it started in earnest.
note: A revenge threat built on defecating on rivals' property, carried by the whole group.

title: Steady Mobbin'
annotation:
In the middle of a day-in-the-life narrative, Cube stops at his mother's house, uses the bathroom, and reports on how much better he feels afterward. Then the day continues.

This is peak early-90s storytelling: nothing is too small to narrate, and the most menacing rapper in America was willing to tell you he needed a minute. Vice called it one of the genre's foundational poop moments.
note: Cube narrates a bathroom stop at his mom's house and the relief that follows.

title: Red Bull
annotation: Redman is the patron saint of gross-out rap, and his guest verse on The W is the canonical crowded-room fart joke: a pun stacked on a pun, delivered at full Funk Doctor energy. Complex ranked it first among the fart-rap anthems, and they were right.
note: A pun-heavy flatulence joke set in a crowded room.

title: So Far...
annotation:
The opening verse is a complete short story: Eminem is on the toilet in a fast-food restaurant, mid-business, when a fan slides a napkin under the door for an autograph. He signs it. Then he uses it.

Over a Joe Walsh sample, no less. It's the most fully realized bathroom scene in his catalog and a contender for the best-written entry on this site.
note: A fan asks for an autograph on a napkin while Em is on a fast-food toilet; the napkin becomes toilet paper.

title: Nasty Boy
annotation:
Biggie's most explicit song is also, briefly, a poop song: a partner makes a request that belongs in this catalog and nowhere else. He delivers it with the same calm authority he brought to everything.

One of the greatest rappers ever, on one of the greatest albums ever. Nobody was above it.
note: A partner's request involving defecation, delivered deadpan on an otherwise sexual track.

title: Boo Boo'n
annotation:
An entire song about sitting on the toilet, from the most laid-back rapper in Houston history. The album cover shows Devin doing exactly that.

Where other rappers use poop as a punchline, Devin treats it as a mood. It's the most relaxed entry on the site and possibly the most honest.
note: A whole song about the act of sitting on the toilet; the album art matches.

title: Did It On'em
annotation:
The hook and the title are the same scatological boast: she did it on them. On them meaning her rivals, and 'it' meaning what you think.

It went platinum. A single from a debut album, built entirely on the image of defecating on one's detractors, went platinum. Nicki learned from Wayne, and the student made it a hit.
note: Title and hook are a boast about defecating on rivals as an act of contempt.

title: Lollipop (Remix)
annotation:
Kanye's remix verse on Wayne's biggest hit contains a skid-mark joke. Two of the most famous rappers alive, on one of the biggest songs of 2008, and the guest verse goes to underwear stains.

Ten years before 'Lift Yourself', the evidence was already there.
note: Kanye's verse includes a skid-mark joke.

title: Shame on a Nigga
annotation:
On the album that changed rap, ODB's verse describes a foul mess lingering in his underwear and compares his reaction to trouble to a bout of diarrhea. In 1993. On the second track.

The Wu-Tang Clan arrived fully formed, and so did Dirty's commitment to the bit.
note: ODB describes a mess in his underwear and compares his temper to uncontrolled diarrhea.

title: E.T. (Extraterrestrial)
annotation: Big Boi drops a bathroom comparison into an otherwise menacing verse, which is the OutKast way: the strangest possible image at the least expected moment. Taking a life and taking a dump, in the same breath, on an album about being an alien in Atlanta.
note: Big Boi compares an act of violence to defecating.

title: Clan in Da Front
annotation: The Genius, the most cerebral member of the Clan, threatens an opponent until they soil themselves. Even GZA, whose verses are chess problems, reached for poop when he needed a threat to land. That tells you everything about its power as a device.
note: GZA threatens a rival to the point of making them soil themselves.

title: Just Lose It
annotation:
The lead single from Encore features an actual fart sound effect worked into the beat, plus a joke about passing gas after a dance move. The video adds visual gags. This was the number-one-selling rapper on earth, launching an album, with flatulence as the hook.

Encore is where Eminem's bathroom humor fully took over. See also 'My 1st Single', two tracks later.
note: A fart sound effect in the production and a joke about passing gas on the dance floor.

title: My 1st Single
annotation: The chorus is built around recorded farting and belching. Not jokes about farting: the sounds themselves, looped, as the hook. Reviewers at the time singled it out as the low point of Encore. We consider it a high point of something else.
note: The hook is made of recorded fart and belch noises.

title: Doo Doo
annotation:
A full song built as one extended feces pun, in the Lil Wayne punchline tradition. The video has New Yorkers on the street singing the hook, which is a sentence that should be read twice.

Troy Ave committed to a concept that most rappers use for one bar and stretched it to three minutes. Respect.
note: An entire song built on an extended doo-doo pun; the video features passersby singing it.

title: Up
annotation:
A number-one single. Cardi explained to Jimmy Fallon, on national television, that the hook's central phrase is a metaphor for a bowel movement that gets stuck partway and won't come out. The audience was not ready. Fallon was not ready.

This makes 'Up' the only song on this site whose poop meaning was revealed on a late-night couch, and the sole holder of the Constipation category's top spot.
note: Cardi told Fallon the hook is a metaphor for a bowel movement that gets stuck and won't come out.

title: Hidden Darts
annotation: A silent-but-deadly aside from one of the most vivid writers in rap, delivered with the same intensity he brings to a crime story. Ghostface doesn't do throwaway lines; even his fart joke has texture.
note: A tongue-in-cheek joke about a silent but smelly fart.

title: Dollar and a Dream III
annotation: On his debut album's opening track, the most earnest rapper of his generation boasts that he can out-fart a rival. The Source flagged this line in 2024 as the apparent template for Ice Spice's 'Think U the Shit (Fart)', which means J. Cole is the godfather of a chart hit about gas. He has never addressed this.
note: A boast about out-farting a rival, later echoed by Ice Spice.

title: The Vapors
annotation: Biz built a career on being gross and lovable. 'The Vapors' is nominally about people who ignored you until you got famous, but Biz can't help himself, and Complex counted its smell joke among the fart-rap anthems. A year later he'd make 'T.S.R.' and go all in.
note: A joke about a bad smell, in a song about fair-weather friends.

title: The Gas Face
annotation: An early entry in the canon. The gas face is the expression you make when something stinks, and the song hands them out to a long list of deserving people, including, famously, MC Hammer. Produced by Prince Paul. A gas-themed hit single in 1989.
note: Title wordplay on gas; the song distributes stink-faces to its enemies.

title: Hot in Herre
annotation: A number-one single for seven weeks whose hook contains a smell joke that an entire country sang along to without thinking about it. Complex counted it. We count it. Nelly has never been asked about it, and that's probably for the best.
note: The hook is built around a smell-based joke.

title: Monopoly
annotation:
Danny Brown is the most gleefully disgusting rapper of his era, and 'Monopoly' is the concentrated dose: he mentions not flushing, he mentions wiping, and he compares rivals to a smell. All in under two minutes, all in that voice.

XXX is one of the best rap albums of the 2010s. This is the track where it stops being polite.
note: Not flushing after urinating, a wiping reference, and a stink comparison aimed at rivals.

title: Grown Up
annotation: A sweet, nostalgic single about growing up in Detroit, with a video starring a child version of Danny. It also contains a boast about eating enormously and then passing a pile of coins. Danny can't do sentiment without a poop joke, and we wouldn't want him to.
note: A boast about eating a huge amount and then defecating money.

title: Blow It Out
annotation: The chorus phrase is a dismissive, gas-adjacent insult, and a verse describes burping and farting away a whole paycheck. Ludacris was the funniest mainstream rapper of the early 2000s and this is him treating bodily functions as a flex.
note: A verse about burping and farting away money; the hook is a gas-adjacent brush-off.

title: Why Stop Now
annotation: Busta boasts that he can defecate and pass gas on the beat and still do damage. This is, technically, a claim about rhythmic ability. It is also the most Busta Rhymes sentence ever constructed.
note: A boast about being able to poop and fart on beat and still kill the track.

title: Pop Ur Shit
annotation: The post-chorus compares the smell of his weed to feces. This is intended as a compliment to the weed. The 2020s have their own grammar of stink, and 21 Savage is fluent.
note: The post-chorus compares the smell of his weed to feces, approvingly.

title: That's That
annotation: The villain, the most quotable writer in underground rap, with lines about cow dung and some crude bowel imagery, stacked in a verse that otherwise references everything from Shakespeare to cereal. DOOM's whole method was that nothing was beneath a good rhyme. Nothing.
note: References to cow dung and crude bowel imagery inside a dense verse.

title: Method Man
annotation: The spoken intro is a torture-threat routine between Method Man and Raekwon, and one of the threats involves sewing a victim's anus shut and continuing to feed him. It is the most anatomically specific constipation reference in rap history, and it's on the song that made Method Man a star.
note: Intro threat about sewing a victim's anus shut and continuing to feed them.

title: Caterpillar
annotation: Eminem's guest verse, a full-speed attack on mumble rap, packs in multiple feces and bowel-movement references, including a line about using the toilet. Vice covered the verse for its anti-mumble-rap content. We covered it for the other thing.
note: Em's verse stacks several feces and bowel references, including a toilet line, while dissing mumble rap.

title: Remind Me
annotation: The punchline comparing a woman's rear end to diarrhea was cited by critic after critic as the low point of Revival, an album that had several candidates. The A.V. Club's review was titled 'Won't the real Slim Shady please grow up'. He did not, and three years later gave us 'Caterpillar'.
note: A widely mocked punchline comparing a rear end to diarrhea.

title: Shake That
annotation: A verse compares a sexual conquest to a toilet seat. Grammy-nominated. With Nate Dogg on the hook. The mid-2000s were a strange time to be the biggest rapper alive.
note: A crude comparison between a conquest and a toilet seat.

title: Stankonia (Stanklove)
annotation: The title track of one of the greatest albums ever made is, per Complex, about how being comfortable enough to stink around someone is a form of love. Stank as intimacy. Only OutKast could make it sound romantic.
note: The premise that being comfortable enough to stink around someone is a sign of love.

title: Toilet Tisha
annotation:
Filed here for the title, with a warning: this is not a joke. 'Toilet Tisha' is a somber story about a pregnant 14-year-old who takes her own life, and the bathroom is where it happens. It's one of the saddest songs OutKast ever made.

It's on the site because the catalog is meant to be complete, and because the same album has 'Stanklove' three tracks earlier. OutKast contained everything.
note: Title-level toilet reference; the bathroom is the setting of a tragedy, not a joke.

title: Definition of Gas
annotation: A Bay Area track built on a running gas pun that doubles as a boast about a smelly reputation. Complex put it on the fart-rap anthems list, and it's the deepest cut there: a regional record whose whole concept is flatulence as a brand.
note: Built on a running gas pun that doubles as a smelly-reputation boast.

title: The Humpty Dance
annotation: Humpty Hump brags about a sexual encounter in a Burger King bathroom. No bodily functions are referenced, which makes this the most borderline entry in the Toilets category, but it is also one of the most famous bathroom scenes in rap, so it stays. Community ruling welcome.
note: A bathroom-set encounter at a Burger King; setting only, no bodily functions.

title: Fuck the World
annotation: The final verse describes farting on a sibling's nose. The song is a list of everything ICP hates, delivered to an arena, and it ends on this. The Juggalos deserved representation on this site and this is it.
note: The last verse describes farting on a sibling's nose.

title: BabyWipe
annotation: The title is a wipe. A line compares the smell of his weed to a fart; another likens the smoke to cat urine. Ski Mask raps like a cartoon and this song is the cartoon's bathroom episode.
note: Title evokes wiping; the weed is compared to a fart.

title: CAPO
annotation: The first verse jokes that lean is upsetting his stomach and making him pass gas. A rare moment of digestive honesty in the drill era.
note: A joke that lean is upsetting his stomach and causing gas.

title: Diaper Money
annotation: A comedy-rap anthem about middle age, in which the great flex is earning enough to cover diapers. It's a joke about rap boasting, performed as rap boasting, so it counts. The top of the Diapers category by a wide margin.
note: Boast-rap about having enough money for diapers, as a middle-aged flex.

title: Mark McGwire
annotation: Future references dealing drugs that have passed through a body. Vice flagged it in their history of poop rap. It's the only entry on the site that is also, technically, a logistics reference.
note: A reference to drugs that have passed through a body before being sold.

title: Toot It and Boot It
annotation: Not about flatulence, but the title is a toot joke whether YG meant it or not, and Complex ruled it eligible. We defer to Complex.
note: Title-level wordplay on tooting.

title: Restroom Occupied
annotation: The restroom is occupied for reasons that have nothing to do with this site's subject matter, but the title alone earns a spot in Toilets. Chris Brown's second appearance in the catalog, both times as a guest on a bathroom-adjacent song. Nobody has asked him about this either.
note: Title-level toilet reference.

title: I Wanna Rock (Doo Doo Brown)
annotation: A Miami bass staple with 'Doo Doo' right there in the parenthetical. Miami New Times put it on their list of the top poop tunes of all time, which is a list that exists.
note: Title references doo doo.

title: Funky Dividends
annotation: A Philly classic whose title, per Complex, is a joke about what happens after late-night eating. One of the best beats of 1989 attached to one of its most dubious puns.
note: Title tied to the digestive aftermath of late-night eating.

title: Started From the Bottom
annotation: Complex counted it as a fart anthem on the strength of a 'bottom' pun. We include it on a provisional basis, pending a ruling from the community, and mostly so Drake has an entry that isn't a Lil Wayne feature.
note: A pun on the word 'bottom'. Borderline eligibility.

title: IANAHB
album: I Am Not a Human Being II
annotation: Over a piano, on the opening track of a major-label album, Wayne describes being wiped after defecating while naked. Vice led its history of poop rap with this line. There is nothing to add.
note: Describes being wiped after defecating, naked, as a boast.

title: Bang Bang
annotation: Wiping and flushing, with the planet Earth cast as the toilet. The mixtape-era Wayne worldview in one image: he is so large that the world is his bathroom.
note: A wipe-and-flush joke that treats the Earth as the toilet.

title: I'm Not Human
album: I Am Not a Human Being
annotation: Wiping with money and throwing it in the bathroom trash. The richest possible version of a toilet joke, from a man who was, at the time, writing from Rikers Island.
note: Wiping with money and discarding it in the bathroom trash.

title: Mr. Carter
annotation: On a track with Jay-Z, Wayne sends his rivals down the drain. Flushing-as-dismissal is one of his favorite moves; Vice counted at least seven flush references in his catalog. This is the one with Jay-Z on it, so it ranks.
note: Flushing rivals down the drain, on a Jay-Z collaboration.

title: Dear Anne (Stan Part 2)
annotation: A sequel to Eminem's 'Stan', a letter to a fan, and it pauses for a scene on the toilet. Wayne will put a bathroom in any song, including a sad one, including one addressed to a person named Anne.
note: Sitting on the toilet, mid-letter to a fan.

title: Money on My Mind
annotation: Wayne addresses a toilet directly, in the second person, on one of Tha Carter II's standout tracks. Few rappers have spoken to more plumbing fixtures, and none with more sincerity.
note: Wayne addresses a toilet directly.

title: I'm Me
annotation: One of the great Wayne boast tracks includes an incontinence joke. Of course it does. This is the song where he declares himself the best rapper alive, and he makes the case with a line about losing control of his bowels.
note: An incontinence joke in the middle of a best-rapper-alive boast.

title: 500 Degreez
annotation: Early-career Wayne, twenty years old, already making stomachache jokes on a title track. The 99 references had to start somewhere.
note: A stomachache joke.

title: Bill Gates
annotation: A pun that connects talking with defecating. Rap has a long tradition of 'talking shit' wordplay; Wayne takes it literally and makes it a bathroom scene.
note: A defecating-to-converse pun.

title: Gonorrhea
album: I Am Not a Human Being
annotation: The title is a different bodily problem, but the poop reference is pure Wayne: a classic 'shitting on rappers' boast, from an album recorded in a sprint before he went to jail.
note: A shitting-on-rappers boast.

title: Green and Yellow
annotation: A Packers anthem recorded for the 2011 Super Bowl, over the 'Black and Yellow' beat, that still finds room to insult someone for not having a bathroom. Green Bay won.
note: A no-bathroom insult in a Super Bowl anthem.

title: HYFR (Hell Ya Fucking Right)
annotation: Wayne's feature on one of Take Care's biggest singles includes a toilet-paper joke. The video is Drake's bar mitzvah. The toilet paper joke is in the bar mitzvah video.
note: A tissue-paper toilet joke in Wayne's verse.

title: I'm Goin' In
annotation: Wayne's verse on the So Far Gone standout narrates a trip to the toilet. So Far Gone has three entries on this site, and all three are Wayne's fault. Drake has never personally written a poop bar; he just keeps inviting the guy who does.
note: Wayne narrates using the toilet.

title: Successful
annotation: An aspirational anthem about wanting the money, cars, and clothes, interrupted by a Wayne smell comparison. The song is about success. The verse is about odor.
note: A smell comparison in Wayne's verse.

title: Ignant Shit
annotation: Over the 'Ignorant Shit' beat, Wayne makes a toilet-paper-and-diarrhea joke. The third So Far Gone entry, and the grossest.
note: A toilet paper and diarrhea joke.

title: Miss Me
annotation: Wayne's verse, recorded shortly before his prison sentence, has a feces-related joke that is not for the faint of heart. He knew he was going away and he made sure to leave one behind.
note: A feces-related sexual joke in Wayne's verse.

title: Roman's Revenge 2.0
annotation: The version of 'Roman's Revenge' where Wayne replaces Eminem, and brings a diaper joke with him. Between this and 'Did It On'em', Pink Friday is quietly one of the great poop albums.
note: A diaper joke in Wayne's verse.

title: Mercy (Remix)
annotation: Wayne boasts about being excrement. In his catalog this is a compliment, and in context it's a brag. Only Wayne can make 'I am poop' sound like a threat.
note: A boast about being excrement.

title: Look at Me Now
annotation: Busta's verse is the famous one. Wayne's verse is the one with the pollution comparison that put it on this site. A number-one rap song with a poop bar, which is less rare than you'd think; see the whole Hall of Fame.
note: Wayne compares something to pollution, scatologically.
